# Overview
Gitboard serves as a local code-change dashboard for GitLab and GitHub, centralizing CI status, open merge requests, and failed job triage alongside local worktree state. It operates by interfacing with local forge CLIs (`gh`, `glab`) and `git` to provide a unified view of development activity.
## Core Objectives
The system is organized around several key functional objectives:
View Aggregation: The `dashboard` component aggregates disparate data sources into a unified interface for developer review.
Process Execution: The `cliexec` module facilitates the execution of external processes, enabling the tool to interact with the local environment and forge tools.
Project Synchronization: Through `syncproj` and `remotegit`, the system maintains alignment between local state and remote repository information.
Automated Triage: The `triage` component assists in identifying and categorizing failed jobs and actionable repository events.
## Component Topology
The product is composed of several specialized internal packages:
`cmd/gitboard`: The primary entrypoint for the application.
`internal/dashboard`: Manages the presentation layer and view aggregation.
`internal/config`: Handles local configuration and settings.
`internal/cliexec`: Provides the interface for executing system commands.
`internal/localgit` & `internal/remotegit`: Manage local and remote Git operations.
`internal/server`: Provides the backend services for the local dashboard.
`internal/syncproj`: Orchestrates project-level synchronization tasks.
`internal/triage`: Implements logic for analyzing and triaging repository signals.
